description: The model's final text on a solution answer must frame the rule's recommendation (lib/advice/recommend.ts), never overrule it, claim eligibility or present an offer. `answers` are scored deterministically by lib/advice/check.test.ts with checkAdviceAnswer over the renovation fixture (lib/advice/fixtures.ts). `live` cases run the real model through runAgent with the same fixture as the compare_routes result: pnpm advice:eval --live (scripts/eval-advice.ts), scored by the same checks plus the number check.

answers.scenario: Frames the rule's pick and the conditional alternative
answers.text: Here are three ways to fund the kitchen. I'd go with Flexicredit over 60 months: the payment stays the same, and the work can start now. Saving first is the better pick if the renovation can wait until next summer.

answers.scenario: Overrules the rule with a shorter term
answers.text: I recommend the 48-month loan instead, since it costs less in total.

answers.scenario: Overrules the rule with saving first, unconditionally
answers.text: You should go with saving up first, it's the cheapest.

answers.scenario: Mentions another route as a trade-off without recommending it
answers.text: Raiffy recommends Flexicredit over 60 months. The 48-month term costs less interest but has a higher payment.

answers.scenario: Recommends while the rule is still waiting for the timing
answers.text: I'd recommend the 60-month Flexicredit. When do you need the money?

answers.scenario: Asks for the timing without recommending
answers.text: Before I recommend a route: when would you like the renovation to start? If it can wait, saving first costs less.

answers.scenario: Claims the customer will be approved
answers.text: I'd go with the 60-month Flexicredit, and you'll be approved easily with your income.
I'd go with the 60-month Flexicredit. I can't say whether you qualify: the bank's assessment decides.

answers.scenario: Presents the simulation as an offer
answers.text: I'd go with the 60-month Flexicredit. This is your offer at 7.90% fixed.

answers.scenario: Says it is not an offer
answers.text: I'd go with the 60-month Flexicredit. It's an indicative simulation, not an offer.

answers.scenario: Can wait a year: frames saving first, the rule's pick
answers.text: Since the work can wait, I'd go with saving first and borrowing the rest later.

answers.scenario: Can wait a year: frames saving first plainly
answers.text: My pick is saving 8 months first, then borrowing 30,000 lei. It costs the least in interest and fees.

live.question: I want to renovate my kitchen for 40,000 lei over 60 months and start right away. I earn 7,800 lei a month, pay 650 lei on other loans and can save 1,250 lei a month.
I'd like 40,000 lei for a kitchen renovation over 60 months. It can wait about a year. I earn 7,800 lei, pay 650 lei on loans and can put aside 1,250 lei a month.
I need 40,000 lei over 60 months to redo the kitchen. I earn 7,800 lei, pay 650 lei on loans and can save 1,250 lei a month.
